steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Component 1 (Portfolio) is worth 60% — it must show a sustained project plus supporting studies that demonstrate all four AOs.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Your portfolio should show a CLEAR NARRATIVE: from starting point, through research and experimentation, to a resolved personal response.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Supporting studies show breadth — additional experiments, artist responses and explorations that complement your main project.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Written annotation must use specialist vocabulary and show REFLECTIVE THINKING — not just descriptions of what you did.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring building your portfolio component 1. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with building your portfolio component 1. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with building your portfolio component 1. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to building your portfolio component 1, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to refi | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
